subject: Orthogonal trace adapter for LlamaIndex - integration scope
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: John Park <john@tracecraft.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Orthogonal trace adapter for LlamaIndex - initial scope

Hi John,

Great to meet you on the call last week — thanks for walking through TraceCraft's tracing SDK and the low-overhead approach you showed. Vanessa and I chatted afterward and we think there's a clean integration path where we can ship an "orthogonal" adapter that lets LlamaIndex customers forward token-level trace events into TraceCraft without changing their prompt code.

High-level proposal (first pass):
- Minimal runtime shim for LlamaIndex that emits span-open/span-close around query/response lifecycle.
- Optional sampling hook (client-configurable) to keep cost predictable.
- Small manifest and config so customers can opt-in per-index.

Open questions we want to align on before a scoped SOW:
1) SDK surface: do you prefer a native Python pip package or instructions for using your existing JS/HTTP collector?
2) Performance targets: our goal is <1ms overhead p95 for per-token emit when sampling=1%. Can TraceCraft confirm ingestion latencies at that rate?
3) Telemetry schema: we'll need a compact event format that includes prefix tokens, request_id, model_version, and optionally embeddings. Can you review the proto?

If you're aligned, Vanessa can draft a technical checklist and Marissa can scope commercial terms. Would you be available for a 30-minute sync Tue 14th PST?

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: John Park <john@tracecraft.io>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@openbridge.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orthogonal trace adapter for LlamaIndex - initial scope

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear note and the great call. Happy to move forward. Quick answers inline: 

1) SDK surface: Python package is ideal given LlamaIndex's user base. We already have a lightweight python client (tracecraft==0.9.2) we can republish as tracecraft-collector. If Redwood would rather call an HTTP collector we can support both, but the pip package will be the path of least friction.

2) Performance: our ingestion pipeline can sustain the sampling scenarios you're targeting. At 1% sampling and token-aware batching we see <5ms median and <25ms p99 for ingest to searchable storage (US-WEST region) — that should be fine for background telemetry; your <1ms overhead is achievable on the client side with non-blocking emit.

3) Telemetry schema: the proto looks reasonable. Two asks from our end:
  - include a stable request_id (UUID) and model hash for cross-lookup
  - redact any PII fields by default; we can offer an inlined transformation hook if customers need to keep some fields for debugging.

We can do Tue 14th 11:00am PT. I'll bring Elena (product) and one of our backend engineers. I'll also share a rough SOW draft and a short demo recording.

Thanks,
John Park
Head of Integrations — TraceCraft

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>
To: John Park <john@tracecraft.io>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orthogonal trace adapter for LlamaIndex - integration checklist

Thanks John — cc'ing Marissa for commercial. A few technical notes to set expectations for the sync: 

- Implementation plan: we'll provide a small shim package (redwood-lindex-trace) that depends on tracecraft-collector when present, otherwise falls back to an HTTP emitter with batched async sends. Shim will be non-blocking and rely on the model's async event loop where possible.
- KV cache visibility: some LlamaIndex connectors use KV caching (prefix caching). We should avoid emitting raw cache contents; instead we'll emit cache keys + hashed token prefixes (deterministic hash) so TraceCraft can reconstruct context without storing PII.
- Sampling controls: we'll expose sampler in four granularity modes: global, per-index, per-user, and adaptive (latency-based).
- Test fixtures: we'll ship a small test corpus and an integration harness that exercises token-level emission under load; we'll share the harness as a Drive link prior to the sync.

Agenda for Tue 11:00 PT:
1) Tech owners introduce (5m)
2) Proto & ingestion constraints (10m)
3) Shim architecture + fallback strategies (10m)
4) Commercial ask and timeline (5m)

See you then — I'll record and drop notes.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Product Manager, Integrations — Redwood Inference

Thanks for the agenda and align — the sync was really helpful. Attached is TraceCraft_SOW_v1.pdf with a narrow pilot scope:
- Deliverables: python collector compatibility, manifest spec, sampling toggle, and three-month joint pilot with up to 10 customers.
- Timeline: 6 weeks to instrument shim + 2 weeks for pilot rollout and telemetry validation.
- Commercials: pilot at no charge; production licensing to be negotiated after pilot (we proposed a per-ingest unit model).

Two immediate action items for Redwood:
1) Confirm that the integration harness and proto will be shared to Drive by EOD Thu (we need it to prep the backend).
2) Confirm an internal review for data retention and privacy — TraceCraft will default to 30-day index retention for pilot unless you request otherwise.

I've attached the SOW (stub) and a short demo recording link in the doc. Happy to iterate.
